newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares' slide still a relief.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares' slide still a relief.

text.p: Belgian shares were in negative territory for the fourth day in succession on Thursday but dealers said it was all part of a normal correction following last week's sharp rise.
"It's a small majority of investors taking profits, it's normal and it's healthy," said Hans Timmerman at brokerage Busschaert.

At 0913 GMT, the Bel-20 index of leading shares was down 0.19 percent, or 4.40 points at 2,343.15 after earlier touching 2,338.30. Timmerman said he saw the next psychological barrier at 2,300 points but real support only at 2,270-2,280.
Steel wire and cord maker Bekaert was a notable gainer with a 2.5 percent rise to 22,675 but Timmerman noted the rise was only fuelled by modest buying orders.
Electronics firm Barco was also firm ahead of the listing of shares in GIMV, the investment company of the Belgian regional government of Flanders, from June 26.
GIMV's main interest is a 33.99 percent stake in Barco, which was up 0.3 percent at 6,770.
Chemicals and drugs firm UCB was down 2.9 percent at 109,750 on continued profit-taking after soaring to 122,000 last week.
